channel.title: Pea OS News
channel.description: What is new on the pea-green desk.

item.title: Meet Pea Flow: objects that travel
item.description:
Pea Flow is a little visual language. Put nodes on the board, drag a wire from an output port to an input port, and press Run.

Every value is a small object you can watch travel along its wire: numbers are blue, text is yellow, yes/no is green or red, and a plain pulse is white.

Start with the example: a clock ticks into a counter, the counter is checked, and lamps light up.

item.title: Pea Records keeps a card file
item.description:
Pea Records is a small database. Define fields, then browse one record at a time: the book in the status area turns back with its upper page and forward with its lower page, and the rail under it jumps anywhere.

List shows the found set as a table (tap a heading to sort). Find narrows it: type >30 into a number, 2026-04-01..2026-04-30 into a date, or part of a word.

item.title: Feeds, from anywhere
item.description:
Pea Feeds reads RSS and Atom. Press Add feed… and paste an address; a web page that announces its feed works too. Subscriptions import and export as OPML.

Requests travel through the Pea OS server on this computer, which is why feeds that a browser page could not read still work.

item.title: Agent Chat talks to any v1 server
item.description:
Agent Chat speaks the common /v1/chat/completions protocol, so it works with a model running on this computer (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM) or a hosted service.

Open Setup, enter the base URL ending in /v1, press Load models, and choose one. With Pea tools on, the agent can open apps and write sticky notes for you.

item.title: Menus learned little pictures
item.description: Menu items now carry small glyphs that stay quiet until you point at them, and show their keyboard shortcuts. The new Window menu acts on the window in front, and Apps are grouped: Create, Organize, Connect, Play, Utilities and System.

item.title: Sticky notes grow up
item.description: Drag a note's corner to resize it. Its header shows its first line, new notes take the next color, and a note can be duplicated or rolled up to its header with a double tap. The Sticky Notes manager shows each note's color and when it was last changed.
